name: PaySpace
description: Cloud payroll and HR, with a payroll engine for each country, about 45 of them, across EMEA and Latin America. Customers run from a one-person shop to bottlers for Heineken and Coca-Cola. South Africa. Deel bought it in March 2024. Deel had been a customer, running payroll in 10 countries on it.

mentions.evidence: TechCrunch, on 5 March 2024, said more than 14,000 customers in 44 countries, with sales growing more than 30 percent a year. The price was not disclosed there. The only outside money named is undisclosed financing from Netcash in 2023. Axios and Calcalist reported a price over $100 million, and that price is the sale, not revenue.
mentions.indieAngle: The biggest customer became the buyer. A single-country filing engine that bigger platforms rent can follow that shape.

whyItPrints: Every country's payroll rules are the moat. They built those engines over about 15 years.
whyThisMatters: Payroll tax is different in every country, and getting it wrong is expensive. PaySpace built about 45 country engines over about 15 years, for customers from a one-person shop up to bottlers for Heineken and Coca-Cola. South Africa. Deel bought it in March 2024. Deel had already been a customer, running payroll in 10 countries on it. A 5 March 2024 TechCrunch piece put the customer count above 14,000, in 44 countries, with yearly sales growth above 30 percent. That article did not give a revenue total or a price. The only outside money it names is undisclosed financing from Netcash in 2023. Axios and Calcalist reported a price over 100 million dollars. That price is what Deel paid. It is not PaySpace's revenue. The page is self-reported, which means the news reports. I did not open the books.
